rejections.reason: Focused Vcur row improved, but same-runner p512 model A/B regressed slightly.
Focused Q4 MUL_MAT_ID default provider passes but is about 10x slower than same-machine Vulkan MoE labels; Q5 MUL_MAT_ID is unsupported.
Both existing staged Q6 MMQL routes passed CPU-reference focused p512 rows but were 4.7x-4.9x slower than the current direct MMQ64 route on result_output.
Vulkan-shaped BM128/BN128/BK_STEP1 staged route passed correctness but took 281.16 ms on p512 result_output versus 94.75 ms for current direct MMQ64.
Column-widened direct route passed correctness but took 194.44 ms on p512 result_output versus 94.75 ms for current direct MMQ64; wider per-thread column work loses on gfx1151.
Focused p33 correctness passed, but same-runner model A/B regressed from 123.074 to 108.935 tok/s; the selector is therefore guarded to n_tokens >= 128.

The wave64 compile of the current Q8_0 packed prompt schedule passed focused CPU-reference rows and selected correctly, but regressed every focused p512 row versus the wave32 object: Vcur 524.0 -> 543.4 us, Qcur 2003.9 -> 2709.9 us, ffn_out 12100.7 -> 18948.8 us, ffn_gate 21138.7 -> 35777.0 us, result_output 203806.5 -> 263176.4 us.

The cooperative A+B LDS staging probe passed focused CPU-reference rows and selected correctly, but regressed every focused p512 row versus the accepted direct-A BM64/BN64 route: Vcur 566.4 -> 684.1 us, Qcur 1940.0 -> 2326.2 us, ffn_out 9800.6 -> 11385.0 us, ffn_gate 8739.3 -> 9634.4 us, result_output 83885.4 -> 91222.7 us.

The smaller per-thread output tile probe passed focused CPU-reference rows and reduced VGPR count from 127 to 78, but regressed p512 total time versus accepted BM64/BN64: Vcur 568.5 -> 660.5 us, Qcur 2817.7 -> 2383.9 us, ffn_out 9915.6 -> 12187.4 us, ffn_gate 9046.7 -> 10254.7 us, result_output 83383.4 -> 91489.5 us.

The BM128/BN64 probe compiled but the public route spills heavily before runtime testing: wavefront_size=32, vgpr_count=192, vgpr_spill_count=47, private_segment_fixed_size=192, group_segment_fixed_size=2176. Do not run focused/model A/B for this spelling.

The Vulkan-large-style BM128/BN128 cooperative A+B staged Q8_0 MMQL probe compiled, but the public route is not viable before runtime testing: wavefront_size=64, group_segment_fixed_size=9216, vgpr_count=192, vgpr_spill_count=472, private_segment_fixed_size=1892. This confirms the naive Q8_0 port of the Q4 MMQL ownership pattern creates excessive live state on gfx1151.

The direct Q8_0 dequant-to-f16 plus F32 RHS cast-to-f16 WMMA route compiled through CMake/Ninja, emitted v_wmma_f32_16x16x16_f16 with no spills (SGPR=20, VGPR=34, LDS=0), and passed CPU-reference focused p512 plus p33/p513 tail rows. It is rejected for production promotion because same-row p512 perf regressed versus the current packed Q8_1 route: 734.75 us for WMMA16 versus 520.69 us for hrx_mul_mat_vec_q8_0_q8_1_x4_mmq128x32_wg256_f32.

The direct Q8_0 dequant-to-f16 plus F32 RHS cast-to-f16 WMMA route using f16 accumulators compiled through CMake/Ninja, emitted v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 with no spills (SGPR=20, VGPR=34, LDS=0), and passed CPU-reference focused p512 plus p33/p513 tail rows. It is rejected for production promotion because same-row p512 perf regressed versus the current packed Q8_1 route: 729.02 us for WMMA16 f16acc versus 521.94 us for hrx_mul_mat_vec_q8_0_q8_1_x4_mmq128x32_wg256_f32.

The 256-thread workgroup aggregation of eight direct Q8_0 f16acc WMMA16 subtiles compiled through CMake/Ninja, emitted v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 with no spills (SGPR=18, VGPR=37, LDS=0), and passed CPU-reference focused p512 plus p33/p513 tail rows. It is rejected for production promotion because same-row p512 perf regressed versus the current packed Q8_1 route and the single-wave WMMA diagnostic: 825.08 us for WG256 f16acc versus 520.35 us for hrx_mul_mat_vec_q8_0_q8_1_x4_mmq128x32_wg256_f32. This shows WG256 grouping without Vulkan-style packed/staged data reuse is not the missing schedule axis.

The Vulkan-oracle staging-depth probe preserved the accepted Q4 BM128/BN128/WG256/WAVE64/TM4/TN2 route and increased BK_STEP from 1 to 2. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with no spills (SGPR=55, VGPR=145, LDS=16384 bytes) and passed p512 plus odd/tail p513 and p33 focused CPU-reference gates. It is rejected for production promotion because the p513 tail A/B was mixed-to-regressive versus BK1: Vcur 207.89 -> 216.53 us, node 886.36 -> 851.36 us, Qcur narrow 42.36 -> 54.21 us, Qcur p513 877.63 -> 1003.39 us. p512 had useful wins on Vcur and node but was flat on Qcur p512, so this axis is not a robust gfx1151 default.

The BM64/BN128 probe kept the accepted BM64 row ownership while widening the column tile toward Vulkan's 128-wide production family. It compiled through CMake/Ninja, but the public route is not viable before runtime testing: wavefront_size=32, group_segment_fixed_size=4352, vgpr_count=192, vgpr_spill_count=55, private_segment_fixed_size=224. This shows the remaining Q8_0 Vulkan-width gap cannot be closed by simple column widening on the direct-A/staged-B scalar-dot schedule.

Exact Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M p512/fa1 Q6 output rows passed focused CPU-reference testing on the current MMQ64 path. The existing wider/staged variants selected correctly but regressed badly: on result_output, current MMQ64 took 375999.17 us, MMQ64x128 took 724312.69 us, and MMQL128 took 1039822.69 us. The legacy-auto perf pass was stopped after several minutes with no CSV output. Treat this as evidence that the Q6 dense-output blocker needs a new schedule/dataflow, not one of the existing opt-in variants.

The direct Q6_K dequant-to-f16 plus F32 RHS cast-to-f16 WMMA route compiled through CMake/Ninja, emitted v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, and has no spills (wave32, SGPR=24, VGPR=35, LDS=0). It passed CPU-reference focused gates for exact Llama 3.1 8B Q4_K_M p512 Q6 rows and synthesized p33/p513 odd-tail rows while selecting the intended provider. It is rejected for production promotion because the focused perf pass failed to finish a useful CSV after several minutes and 1688 selected dispatches, while the current MMQ64 route completed the same exact rows at 2254.51 us, 56728.72 us, and 379448.50 us. This proves the lane mapping and WMMA opcode path but not the Vulkan-style staged 128x128/256-thread dataflow needed for throughput.

The direct Q4_K dequant-to-f16 plus F32 RHS cast-to-f16 staged-WG256 WMMA route was added as a Vulkan-oracle diagnostic after RADV evidence showed matmul_q4_k_f32_f16acc_aligned_l emits v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 while the current HRX Q4 MMQL128 route emits integer v_dot4_i32_iu8. It compiled through CMake/Ninja, emitted v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16, and has no spills (wave32, SGPR=27, VGPR=53, LDS=3072). It passed CPU-reference focused DeepSeek R1 Qwen 14B Q4_K_M rows for p512 and exact odd/tail p33/p513 while selecting the intended provider. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed badly versus the accepted packed Q8_1 MMQL128 route: Kcur 986.46 -> 2402.45 us, Qcur 4123.76 -> 14151.28 us, ffn_out 13126.86 -> 55425.92 us, ffn_gate 13244.67 -> 58826.01 us. This proves that matching the WMMA opcode without Vulkan-like packed/staged reuse is insufficient on gfx1151.

The Vulkan-large Q4_K direct-F32 RHS WMMA probe cloned the resolved oracle class more closely than the earlier 64x32 direct WMMA diagnostic: BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, Q4_K dequant to f16 LDS, F32 RHS cast to f16 LDS, and multiple 16x16 f16acc WMMA accumulator tiles per workgroup. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave32, SGPR=38, VGPR=115, LDS=16384) and emitted 16 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites. It passed CPU-reference focused DeepSeek Q4_K p512 rows, exact p513 tail rows, and kept p33 on the existing narrow route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 979.20 -> 1565.46 us, Qcur 3948.47 -> 6674.58 us, ffn_out 14573.74 -> 19495.02 us, ffn_gate 13196.74 -> 23377.37 us. This rules out the simple direct-f32-RHS HIP WMMA clone; the remaining gap is likely in RADV's cooperative-matrix lowering, LDS padding/stage layout, vectorized global/LDS scheduling, or explicit Q8_1 packing reuse rather than the high-level tile alone.

The VK128 padded probe isolated the Vulkan LDS padding axis by keeping the rejected direct-F32 Q4_K WMMA shape (BM128/BN128/BK32/WG256, f16acc WMMA) but changing the A/B shared-memory row stride from 32 halfs to Vulkan's 40-half f16vec2-equivalent stride. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave32, SGPR=25, VGPR=121, LDS=20480) and emitted 16 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites. It passed focused p512 and exact p513 CPU-reference rows while selecting the padded provider, and p33 stayed on the existing narrow route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 987.01 -> 1543.83 us, Qcur 4107.51 -> 7244.42 us, ffn_out 15515.40 -> 24740.20 us, ffn_gate 12186.69 -> 25907.86 us. Padding alone does not recover the RADV coopmat schedule; the next Q4 work should stop cloning direct-F32 HIP WMMA at this level and either reproduce RADV's lower-level cooperative-matrix scheduling much more exactly or return to packed Q8_1/x4 reuse.

The RADV-schedule prefetch probe preserved the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 WMMA shape and explicitly loaded both k-half A/B fragments before issuing WMMA to move toward the Vulkan large coopmat LDS-load-before-WMMA cadence. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave32, SGPR=25, VGPR=133, LDS=20480) and emitted 16 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites, 18 ds_loads, 2 ds_stores, 8 global loads, 64 global stores, and 38 s_waitcnts. A direct wave64 variant could not compile because the ROCm WMMA builtin requires wavefrontsize32. The prefetch route passed p512 and exact p513 CPU-reference rows while selecting the intended provider, and exact p33 stayed on the existing narrow route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 990.28 -> 1508.75 us, Qcur 4038.39 -> 7253.08 us, ffn_out 15180.79 -> 25845.81 us, ffn_gate 13737.11 -> 25565.23 us. Source-level prefetching changed wait placement and pressure but still did not reproduce RADV's 32-static-WMMA / 192-ds-load cooperative-matrix lowering.

The pair64 ownership probe preserved the rejected VK128 padded direct-F32 WMMA shape but remapped two wave32 waves to one Vulkan-style 64x64 output owner, matching the specialized Vulkan coopmat ownership more closely than the previous 16x128 wave striping. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave32, SGPR=25, VGPR=134, LDS=20480) and emitted 16 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites, 12 ds_loads, 2 ds_stores, 8 global loads, 64 global stores, and 28 s_waitcnts. The route passed p512 and exact p513 CPU-reference rows while selecting the intended provider, and exact p33 stayed on the existing narrow route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 979.99 -> 1449.28 us, Qcur 3955.07 -> 7255.33 us, ffn_out 15772.01 -> 24397.54 us, ffn_gate 12102.39 -> 25685.38 us. Wave-pair output ownership alone does not recover RADV's subgroup-64 cooperative-matrix lowering; the HIP builtin still lowers as independent wave32 WMMA owners with far shallower LDS traffic.

The true wave64 WMMA probe used the ROCm __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16_w64 builtin rather than compiling the wave32 builtin in wave64 mode. It follows the AMD matrix-instruction-calculator RDNA3 mapping for A/B fragments and D stores, preserves the VK128 padded direct-F32 shape, and compiles through CMake/Ninja with no spills (wave64, SGPR=29, VGPR=165, LDS=20480). The generated ISA is the closest direct-WMMA match so far: 32 static v_wmma_f16_16x16x16_f16 sites, 32 ds_loads, 2 ds_stores, 8 global loads, 64 global stores, 155 s_waitcnts. The first implementation accidentally used a wave32 lane id in wave64 mode and failed correctness; after fixing lane ids to 0..63, both low-half and high-half OPSEL routes passed p512 CPU-reference rows while selecting correctly, and the low route passed exact p513 with exact p33 staying on the existing narrow route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 972.56 -> 1535.23 us low / 1503.17 us high, Qcur 3943.78 -> 8354.39 us low / 8357.47 us high, ffn_out 14110.24 -> 26927.58 us low / 27073.09 us high, ffn_gate 12483.27 -> 27026.65 us low / 26952.06 us high. Wave64 WMMA correctness and 32-static-WMMA structure are now proven, but this direct-F32 dataflow remains too slow versus packed Q8_1.

The packed-Q8_1/x4 output-ownership probe kept the Q4_K MMQL staged packed dataflow, BM128, wave64, and BK_STEP1, but narrowed the column tile from BN128/WN64 to BN64/WN32. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with lower pressure than the current MMQL128 route (wave64, SGPR=53, VGPR=109 versus 139, LDS=5632 versus 8192, no spills) and halved static dot/store sites. It passed focused p512 and exact p513 CPU-reference rows while selecting the intended provider, and p33 stayed on the existing MMQ64 route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 989.40 -> 1100.29 us, Qcur 4018.51 -> 4817.41 us, ffn_out 14563.47 -> 22394.71 us, ffn_gate 14017.86 -> 20459.41 us. Lowering accumulator footprint alone loses because it doubles the column workgroups and likely reduces B reuse; the Q4 packed path should keep the 128-column tile unless a future schedule also improves load/wait behavior.

The packed-Q8_1/x4 LDS-resource probe preserved the current Q4_K MMQL128 production dataflow, BM128, BN128, wave64, BK_STEP1, and output ownership, but padded shared A-cache rows from 24 to 32 bytes and packed-B cache rows from 40 to 64 bytes. This explicitly tested the Vulkan oracle's larger padded LDS/resource axis without changing column reuse. It compiled through CMake/Ninja with wave64, SGPR=52, VGPR=145, LDS=12288, no spills, and almost unchanged static schedule shape versus current MMQL128: 512 v_dot sites, 46 ds_loads, 12 ds_stores, 18 global loads, 64 global stores, 184 s_waitcnts, and 2 barriers. The route selected correctly for p512 and p513, passed focused CPU-reference rows for p512 and p513, and kept exact p33 on the existing MMQ64 route. It is rejected for production promotion because same-runner p512 focused perf regressed versus current MMQL128 on every row: Kcur 979.58 -> 1326.86 us, Qcur 4108.71 -> 5317.20 us, ffn_out 13816.55 -> 17334.05 us, ffn_gate 12309.63 -> 15366.25 us. Padding the packed-cache rows raises LDS/VGPR pressure but does not materially improve the LDS wait schedule; future packed-path work should target actual LDS-read issue order, B-cache ownership, or instruction scheduling instead of row padding alone.
